visualLanguage: design_system/public/PUBLIC_UI.md (locked 2026-08-11). The index.html in this directory is the RETIRED KB-era mockup and is kept only because ci:mockup-coverage requires a parity.json beside any index.html. It is not the visual target for this route any more. The target is the six closed patterns in PUBLIC_UI.md, built from components/site/v3.
competitiveTarget: Long-tail SEO: 'homes for sale in {zip}'. Beat the portals on the same query by answering it in the first viewport with five live figures under ONE source trace, then handing over the whole ZIP as map plus list in one frame where every row and every pin is a door. No aggregator prints the query behind the number, and none of them says which figures it does not have.
note: PUBLIC_UI.md §3 (2026-08-14). Zip uses the city opening: Field of this ZIP's houses. Count is a caption, never a number hero. Child plats are doors below the fold. Order is Breadcrumb (Home / Cities / city / ZIP), Field (map plus list, one set), Instrument level 1 (pace below the fold, no inventory hero), Ledger (neighborhoods), Sheet (listing alerts), Ledger (nearby), Footer. ONE getZipListings call. Absent is not zero. No MoS at ZIP scope.
deletions: KbHero: the dark photo hero, its property-search field, and its voice-search button. With it goes the getSurfaceImage('hero') read, because nothing renders a photo now. The hero's lede figures survive as the Instrument's figures.

KbMarketHud: the market HUD. Its four live tile figures survive in the Instrument. Its 13-month trend chart and 5-year year-series do NOT: they were the PARENT CITY's price history, a different population from this page, and the KB page relabeled them rather than dropping them. The getPriceHistory read, the buildYearSeries call, and ZIP_CITY_SLUG (which existed only to address that city row) are deleted with it. Its footnote also printed the full months-of-supply methodology and threshold sentence on a page whose monthsSupply was null.

KbFeatured: the 14-tile featured rail, its listing photography, its background-video and tour badges, and the resolveFeaturedItems + getListingVideos work behind them. The Field's rows carry the same homes as text. Its 'See all {n} {city} homes for sale' label is also gone, which fixes a mislabeled figure: {n} was the ZIP's active count printed beside the CITY's name.

KbListingMap: replaced by PlaceFieldMap (app/central-oregon/_v3/PlaceFieldMap.client.tsx) in the Field's map slot. Same population and same framing. Dropped with the KB component: the marker clusterer, close-zoom photo-stamp icons, the InfoWindow card, and the region town and peak labels. The route-local ZipFieldMap pair was deleted once this shared map existed.

KbCommunityAlerts: replaced by ZipAlertsSheet on V3Sheet. The capture contract is unchanged (see dataLayer), including the hidden `company` honeypot, which is a real control again through V3Sheet's sheet-level `trap` prop after shipping briefly as a hardcoded empty string. All five defences run: honeypot, per-IP rate limit, email validation, native dedup, compliance gate. The email control accepts 254 characters, the bound the server action itself applies. The standing disclosure ('One email per new listing. Unsubscribe from any of them.') sits beside the field at the point of capture, as the KB band printed it. Dropped: the 'Sign in to manage alerts' link in the confirmation fine print.
KbSell: the seller band and its address-prefill field. Seller lives on Sell. The Instrument ghost is All homes in {zip} through zipSearchHref.
MarketSources: the Oregon Data Share citation band. Every source line on the page now names Oregon Data Share inside the trace for the figures it covers.
SmoothScrollProvider: the Lenis wrapper. The v3 register does not hijack scroll.
KbFooter and KbBreadcrumb: replaced by V3Footer and V3Breadcrumb.
The '0 Active' count that the KB page printed on all nine other-ZIP cards. This page has not queried those ZIPs, so it prints no count beside them.

requiredComponents.name: MetadataBlock
requiredComponents.section: BreadcrumbList + Place + Dataset JSON-LD. Emitted here because V3Breadcrumb carries no structured data of its own, on purpose, so one derivation feeds the visible figures and the markup. Required by ci:ai-structured-data for this route by name.

requiredComponents.name: KbNav
requiredComponents.section: The public header, mounted by app/layout.tsx through PublicNav. Not a page-level import; ci:mockup-parity auto-satisfies this entry while the layout owns the header. The chrome has not migrated yet, so this route is a mixed page in the ci:public-ui ledger by design.

requiredComponents.name: KbSectionTracker
requiredComponents.section: Page-level analytics, pageType='zip'. Kept on the KB register deliberately: section tracking is analytics wiring, not visual language, and the barrel ships no equivalent. ci:kb-page-contract accepts either register's tracker, and the tracker's observer reads both registers' sections.

requiredComponents.name: V3Breadcrumb
requiredComponents.section: Chrome. Home > Cities > {city} > {zip}. Surface tone: this page opens on a Field, not a dark Stage.

requiredComponents.name: V3Instrument
requiredComponents.section: Pattern 1, once, level 1, BELOW the fold. H1 head term over median list, price per sq ft, days on market, and new-in-30. The inventory integer is the Field caption, not a hero here. Ask is a ghost into the same ZIP set.

requiredComponents.name: V3Field
requiredComponents.section: Pattern 2, once, the opening. The ZIP's whole active inventory as map plus list in one frame. Caption counts that same set. No V3Figure inventory hero.

requiredComponents.name: PlaceFieldMap
requiredComponents.section: The real Google map in the Field's map slot, shared at app/central-oregon/_v3/PlaceFieldMap.client.tsx. Pins come from fieldMapPins(fieldItems), the same set the list renders. Hovering a row lights its pin through useV3FieldBinding. Place.hasMap ships when at least one pin plots. The route-local ZipFieldMap pair is gone.

requiredComponents.name: V3Ledger
requiredComponents.section: Pattern 3, twice, never adjacent to each other. Neighborhoods: the top eight subdivision groups by count from the same tiles, when = homes for sale in that group, value = that group's median list price, with its own trace naming the grouping. A GROUP IS KEYED BY THE RAW FEED VALUE AND LABELLED BY A NAME. neighborhoodName() in _v3/zip-constants.ts decides whether the MLS SubdivisionName is a name a visitor can read: it runs displaySubdivision first (so a masked *** or n/a. value cannot enter through the Ledger after being dropped from the tiles), then the noise set, then rejects any value holding an underscore because that is a field code and no spelled name in this feed carries one, then writes out the one abbreviation the repo already records, Crr = Crooked River Ranch (lib/data/geo/report-cities.ts, data/resort-communities.json), keeping whatever the feed appended verbatim. Before it, /zip/97760 published 'Crr3_C' as a neighborhood with a median beside it. Listings whose value is not a name stay inside the ZIP count and are counted in the section's note, never silently dropped. The label never touches the door: each row's door and the section's 'All homes in {zip}' action both go through zipSearchHref (see doors) carrying the RAW subdivision value, so a row's count and its destination's count stay the same number. Nearby: plain rows with NO value column and therefore no source line, carrying the parent city's inventory page and the other nine canonical ZIPs in the canonical order.

requiredComponents.name: ZipAlertsSheet
requiredComponents.section: Pattern 5, once, in app/zip/[zip]/_v3/ZipAlertsSheet.client.tsx. The page's one filled ask, anchored at #get-alerts as the KB band was. Wraps V3Sheet and calls the same server action with the same payload (see dataLayer).

requiredComponents.name: V3Quiet
requiredComponents.section: Pattern 6, only in the degraded branch, where it replaces the Instrument and states that the listing feed did not answer. The Instrument does not render in that branch, so the page is still four of six patterns either way. A section that cannot source a figure says why instead of printing a zero.

requiredComponents.name: V3Footer
requiredComponents.section: Chrome. The canonical sitemap projection (V3_FOOTER_COLUMNS off lib/site-nav) plus the legal row. Carries no button. The first viewport is the Field. Rendered OUTSIDE <main>, because HTML-AAM maps <footer> to role=contentinfo only when it is not nested in sectioning content.

layoutComponents.name: PublicNav
layoutComponents.note: Resolves to KbNav today. Not in requiredComponents as itself because the gate checks the route file; the KbNav entry above is the one the gate auto-satisfies.

deferredComponents.name: V3Stage
deferredComponents.reason: Pattern 4 needs an owned video or photo and is never allowed over a number. PUBLIC_UI.md §3 opens a ZIP on the Field of this ZIP's houses. Adding a Stage would also pull this route into ci:kb-breadcrumb-overlay's dark-opening arm, which would then require tone="on-media" on the breadcrumb.

routeContract.generateStaticParams: Required. Maps CANONICAL_ZIPS in order: 97701, 97702, 97703, 97756, 97759, 97739, 97707, 97741, 97754, 97760. A ZIP outside the set 404s rather than prerendering an empty page. ci:static-params and ci:sitemap-resolvable (family 'zip') both bind this route.
routeContract.param: zip, normalized to its five digits before the canonical-set check, in both generateMetadata and the page.

required.emittedBy: MetadataBlock schemas array (breadcrumb entry): Home, Cities, {city}, {zip}
MetadataBlock schemas array (place entry), with the ZIP as postalCode

MetadataBlock schemas array (dataset entry). The same five variables in the same order with the same names and unitText: Active single-family listings, Median list price, Median price per sq ft, Median days on market, New listings last 30 days. Unrounded values, as before. The one change is that a variable the read could not source is now absent rather than zero.

jsonLd.note: One derivation. The Instrument's figures and the Dataset's variables are computed once, from one query, in one place, so a figure and its variable can never come from different reads. They are not always the same STRING: the median list price prints through formatPrice, the site-wide display convention CLAUDE.md section 0 sanctions ('$474,500 to $475K is fine'), while the variable carries the unrounded value the query returned. Stated here so nobody reads 'one derivation' as a promise that the payload echoes the printed digits.

doors.valuation: Seller lives on Sell. This route no longer mounts a valuation primary. The Instrument ghost and the Field rows go through zipSearchHref.
doors.rule: A count that links somewhere claims that somewhere holds it, so a figure's door is checked the way a number is. Every door out of a figure on this page carries this page's exact population — active, PropertyType 'A', postalCode = this ZIP — and each of the three params is load-bearing. postalCode is the real searchListingsAll filter, the same one the alert payload sends. propertyType=A is this page's scope: without it 97756 answers 474 against the page's 392 and 97754 answers 405 against 217, because a ZIP also holds land, manufactured, and income rows. view=list is what makes the count comparable: the default split view defaults its city to Bend (app/search/page.tsx) and counts only what the map viewport holds, which empties every non-Bend ZIP and clipped 97703 to 241 against its 256.
doors.regression: The KB page hung '?keywords={zip}' on its subdivision CTA and the migration carried it onto the LEAD FIGURE and the neighborhood Ledger action. keywords is free text, not a ZIP filter: /search 308s to /homes-for-sale, the split view applies its Bend default, and nine of the ten canonical ZIPs landed on an empty result set under a live Oregon Data Share trace. 97703 disagreed quantitatively instead, 256 against 241. Fixed 2026-08-12.
doors.verification: Production, browser UA, count for count. Ten ZIPs: 97701 207, 97702 402, 97703 256, 97756 392, 97759 181, 97739 244, 97707 248, 97741 102, 97754 217, 97760 72 — each equal to the figure the page prints. Eight neighborhood rows on 97703: 16, 15, 11, 11, 10, 8, 7, 7 — each equal to its row.

dataLayer.getZipListings: lib/data/listings/getListingTiles.ts, wrapped in withTimeoutFallbackResult (5s). listing_tile_mv, postalCode={zip}, status='active', propertyType='A', limit 5000. THE ONLY READ ON THIS PAGE. It feeds the Instrument, the Field and its map, the neighborhood Ledger, and the Dataset JSON-LD. The result's ok flag is the difference between an empty ZIP and a feed that did not answer, and every figure is gated on it.
dataLayer.submitSearchAlertSignup: app/actions/search-alert-capture.ts, bound to ZipAlertsSheet. UNCHANGED CONTRACT: { email, filters: { city: ZIP_CITY_NAME[zip], propertyType: 'A', postalCode: zip }, company }. Same listing_alerts row, same lead, same compliance gate. On success it still fires the same two residuals with the same arguments: rememberGuestWatch(buildGuestWatchFromPlace({ communityName: `ZIP ${zip}`, city, extraFilters })) and fireSearchEvent('alert_create', buildAlertCreatePayload('daily')).
dataLayer.note: Route-local constants and pure helpers (the canonical ZIP set and its order, the area labels, the parent city names, the subdivision noise list, normalizeZip, median, neighborhoodName, isFigure, numeric, tileTitle, tileMeta, zipSearchHref) live in app/zip/[zip]/_v3/zip-constants.ts so the route file stays under the ci:file-size-budget floor. ZIP_CITY_NAME is a payload value, not a display string. Nothing is fetched that this page does not render.
